notes: S.N.162 FLAGGED CASE per BRIEF.md: bhv.fr was already characterized in this project's memory as a site-wide Cloudflare managed challenge, with a verified retry map (French category taxonomy recovered from the Wayback CDX index) sitting in pipeline/c37.json's notes field (that S.N.37 slot is actually Frontgate; the BHV content is a carry-forward note, not a real prior extraction -- pipeline/c37.json itself has status='failed', rows=[] for BHV, i.e. no qty was ever obtained for this company before). Read that notes field first as instructed. THIS SESSION'S ACCESS ATTEMPT (fresh, independent of the old c37 attempt): robots.txt, apex '/', and '/c/maison' all returned the Cloudflare interstitial (title 'Just a moment...', meta robots noindex/nofollow, CSP referencing challenges.cloudflare.com) with HTTP 403 and header cf-mitigated:challenge. Ran the full Rule 2 sweep again: (1) direct fetch -- 403; (2) curl_cffi impersonation across 8 profiles (chrome124/131/120/123, safari18_0/17_0, firefox135, edge101) -- 403 + cf-mitigated:challenge on every single one; (3) r.jina.ai reader proxy on /c/maison -- 403, same Cloudflare interstitial body relayed through the proxy; (4) translate.goog -- 403, same interstitial; (5) WebFetch -- 403 Forbidden, no body; (6) api.allorigins.win third-party proxy -- HTTP 522 (origin unreachable via that proxy). No browser automation was used per Rule 2's explicit prohibition (shared-browser pool). CONCLUSION: the block is byte-for-byte the same site-wide Cloudflare managed challenge documented in c37.json's failure_reason (which additionally exhausted Playwright/playwright-stealth/patchright real-browser attempts in an earlier session) -- confirms it is still fully in force today, not transient. STRUCTURE-RECOVERY WORKAROUND USED (new this session, not in the old c37 notes): Google's site-index (WebSearch 'site:bhv.fr "<path fragment>"') returns real, currently-indexed bhv.fr category URLs even though the URLs themselves 403 on direct fetch -- i.e. Googlebot's crawl (with Google's own IP/allowlist) gets past the challenge even though nothing available to this worker does. This let me confirm ~20 real, currently-live leaf-category URLs matching the qualifying decor branches named in c37.json's retry map (arts de la table / luminaire / decoration), rather than having to guess URL slugs. IMPORTANT CAVEAT -- WebSearch's prose summaries of these results included apparent product-count numbers (e.g. '72,929 items filtered by Hay brand', '39,000 red table lamps', '19,168 products from Reality brand') that are implausible for a single mid-size French department store category and inconsistent with smaller counts shown for adjacent brand/color filters (single digits to low hundreds) in the SAME result sets -- this proves the search-summarization layer fabricates/hallucinates numeric detail at least some of the time. Per the project's zero-estimate rule, NONE of these WebSearch-derived numbers were used as qty evidence anywhere in this file; every qty below is null, sourced only from a confirmed-blocked live fetch. Tried a Bing HTML search and an r.jina.ai proxy of a Google results page to see raw snippet text as an alternative to the summarized WebSearch output (hoping for a literal 'N produits' string) -- Bing returned no organic bhv.fr result rows in the raw HTML (JS-rendered), and Google's search page itself 403'd through r.jina.ai -- neither yielded independently-verifiable count text, so the null+flag determination stands. STRUCTURE (translated to English, hierarchy per brief): Lighting -- Pendant & Ceiling Lights, Lamps (Table/Bedside/Desk), Wall Lights & Sconces, Floor Lamps, Reading Lights, Spotlights & Track Lighting, Outdoor Lighting, and Bathroom Lighting (RULE 0 GAIN -- see below). Wall Decor & Mirrors -- Mirrors, Wall Art & Prints, Photo Frames, Decorative Wall Elements, Wall Objects, and Clocks (RULE 0/BRIEF GAIN -- see below). Home Accessories -- Vases, Candle Holders/Photophores & Lanterns, Decorative Objects & Figurines, Baskets. Kitchen & Dining -- Dinnerware, Glassware, Carafes, Table Accessories & Serveware, Tea & Coffee Service. RULE 0 GAINS OVER THE OLD c37.json RETRY MAP: the old notes told a future retry to keep 'luminaire de salle de bain (bathroom)' and 'decoration-murale-horloge (clocks)' EXCLUDED, following an earlier project convention that predates this batch's Rule 0. This batch's Rule 0.1 explicitly puts room-organised lighting (incl. bathroom) in scope, and the brief's own INCLUDE list explicitly names 'Clocks (all types)' as in scope -- both are added as new rows here, each flagged inline explaining the correction. EXCLUSIONS MAINTAINED from the old c37.json retry map (all still judged out of scope under this batch's rules too): maison-culinaire (cookware/kitchen tools), maison-gros electromenager (large appliances), maison-mobilier / maison-jardin-mobilier de jardin (furniture), maison-literie (bedding), maison-linge de maison + decoration-coussin plaid et couvre-lit / rideau et store / tapis (textiles), decoration-quincaillerie decorative (hardware), decoration-murale-papier peint / stickers / rouleau adhesif / cimaises / corniches / accessoires d'encadrement (wallpaper/home-improvement, both explicitly excluded categories per this brief too), bougie et parfum d'interieur (home fragrance + scented candles -- explicitly excluded per this brief), decoration-objet+deco-decoration+de+fete (party/holiday decor -- 'Holiday & Gift' explicitly excluded per this brief). NEW EXCLUSION JUDGEMENT CALL made this session: 'autour du vin' (wine accessories: carafe a decanter, seau a glace/ice bucket, shaker cocktail/cocktail shaker) was in the old retry map's qualifying list but is dropped here as bar tools, on direct precedent from c37.json/Frontgate which dropped 'Barware & Wine Accessories' (shakers, tongs, openers) as excluded bar tools under this same project's kitchen-tools exclusion; its one legitimately decorative item (decanter/carafe) is already covered by the standalone Carafes row. 'plante et fleur' (plants & flowers, named inside the old 'objet deco' bucket) is excluded per this brief's explicit 'artificial/faux plants & flowers' exclusion. Company/duplicate determination: BHV Marais Maison is not flagged elsewhere in this batch as a duplicate of any other roster row; its own duplicate risk is inherent in this S.N.'s carry-forward note (an early-batch mis-slotting under S.N.37, corrected here as S.N.162's own extraction).
